title: Built for the Talkies

body: The Tivoli opened on Christmas Day 1928 as one of the first theaters in the country designed from the start for sound films, arriving only a year after "The Jazz Singer" proved that audiences wanted to hear the movies. Its Renaissance Revival auditorium and street-front marquee were built for a suburb that wanted a downtown worth staying in after dark. The theater has run continuously since, and today it is operated by Classic Cinemas, which has owned it since 1978.

topics.name: Downtown After Dark
topics.description: Theaters, marquees, music, and the nightlife that gave the village a reason to gather after the last train home.

topics.name: Rail and the Commuter Town
topics.description: How the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy line turned a farm settlement into a railroad suburb, and how the daily commute still shapes downtown.
